tests.name: Vivid color coverage, hue and compatibility

bounds: Full Windows x64 WinExe compiled. An identical production-component wake harness passed 34/34 cases on this candidate and 24/34 on its baseline. Retained and additional isolated Windows suites passed. A Combined fixture initially hit a path-length limit; unchanged fixture/source passed from a shorter evidence path. Actual CLR smoothing matched output bytes and retained double bits across 66,527 frames; allocation audit removed 1,440 bytes per 18-zone update. These use generated pixels, injected time/capture and fake transports; delivery/firmware models are not physical measurements. Native DLL and source are unchanged and were not rebuilt. Sleep/wake, flashes, optical color matching, game performance and uninterrupted operation are not established.
changes: Three wake-only power-on then stream-enable attempts at least one second apart within a six-second episode, with retained own-off authority and cancellation/fresh-image checks.
Separate wake recovery from standby, no periodic healthy-playback mode reset.
Equivalent scalar smoothing removes 36 temporary integer arrays per 18-zone update.
Add dated power, wake state and distinct owned/requested cleanup diagnostics.
Color algorithm/settings unchanged from local 0.1.5; current optical acceptance unresolved.

tests.name: Independent numeric and concurrent gamma audit

previousReleaseValidation.bounds: Current managed calibration and integration checks use generated pixels, injected clock/transport and isolated settings. Independent numeric/concurrent checks are separate arithmetic validation, not additional engine cases. Native DLL and shader are byte-identical to v0.1.3 and were not rebuilt; nine generated WARP red-color comparisons were run during diagnosis. Previous release tests and physical off/resume evidence are historical, not rerun or new physical acceptance. No exact display/strip color match or long-duration stability is established.
